def: Arrest of inspiration when the examiner presses under the right costal margin, a sign of acute cholecystitis.
Paralysis of cranial nerves IX, X and XI from a lesion at the jugular foramen, causing dysphagia, hoarseness and trapezius and sternocleidomastoid weakness.
An infant's startle response in which the arms abduct and extend then draw together; it normally disappears by about 3-6 months and persistence suggests neurologic damage.
An electric shock sensation running down the spine on neck flexion, seen in multiple sclerosis, cervical cord disease and B12 deficiency.
Benign pigmented iris hamartomas that are a hallmark of neurofibromatosis type 1.
Macrophages lining the liver sinusoids that clear bacteria and debris from portal blood.
Golden-brown rings of copper deposited in the periphery of Descemet membrane of the cornea, characteristic of Wilson disease.
The part of the lesser omentum running from the liver to the lesser curvature of the stomach; it carries the left and right gastric arteries.
Bony enlargements of the distal interphalangeal joints in osteoarthritis.
Bony enlargements of the proximal interphalangeal joints in osteoarthritis.
Older name for reactive arthritis, the triad of arthritis, urethritis and conjunctivitis after an infection, associated with HLA-B27.
Tingling in the distribution of a nerve when it is tapped, such as over the wrist in carpal tunnel syndrome; indicates nerve irritation or regrowth.
Buttock pain and sciatica-like symptoms attributed to the piriformis muscle compressing the sciatic nerve.
The pelvis drops on the side opposite the stance leg when standing on one leg, from weakness of the gluteus medius and minimus (superior gluteal nerve) on the stance side.
Red linear streaks in skin folds, such as the antecubital fossa, in scarlet fever.
Inhibitory interneurons in the spinal ventral horn that receive collaterals from alpha motor neurons and feed back glycinergic inhibition onto them; tetanus toxin blocks their transmitter release.
Infection by Rickettsia, obligate intracellular bacteria spread by arthropod vectors, causing fever, headache and rash, as in Rocky Mountain spotted fever and typhus.
Severe leptospirosis with jaundice, kidney failure and bleeding, from Leptospira in water contaminated with rat urine.
A five-stage scale of pubertal development based on breast, genital and pubic hair changes.

Lateral medullary infarction (usually PICA or vertebral artery) causing ipsilateral facial pain and temperature loss, Horner syndrome, dysphagia and ataxia, with contralateral body pain and temperature loss.
Rapid gastric emptying after gastric surgery, causing early cramping and diarrhea from osmotic fluid shifts and late hypoglycemia.
Clonal bone marrow disorders with ineffective, dysplastic blood cell production, causing cytopenias and a risk of progression to acute myeloid leukemia.
Renal artery stenosis, from atherosclerosis in older adults or fibromuscular dysplasia in young women, causing hypertension via renin-angiotensin activation.
An infantile epilepsy of spasms, hypsarrhythmia on EEG and developmental regression; associated with tuberous sclerosis and treated with ACTH or vigabatrin.
A tumor arising from primordial germ cells in the gonads or midline, including seminoma, dysgerminoma, teratoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma and embryonal carcinoma.
The knee-jerk reflex tested by tapping the patellar tendon, mediated by the femoral nerve (L2-L4).
Persistent headache, dizziness, poor concentration and irritability for weeks after a head injury.
A scoring system of cervical dilation, effacement, station, consistency and position that predicts the likelihood of successful labor induction.
Tuberculous infection of the vertebrae, usually thoracolumbar, causing back pain, vertebral collapse and kyphosis.
The embryonic tract from the foramen cecum of the tongue down to the thyroid; a remnant forms a midline neck cyst that moves with swallowing and tongue protrusion.
The remnant of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct in females, running along the uterus and vagina; cysts form in the anterolateral vaginal wall.
An intraepithelial adenocarcinoma of apocrine-rich skin (vulva, perianal region, scrotum) presenting as a red, scaly, itchy plaque with Paget cells.
Concentric, laminated calcified spherules seen in papillary thyroid carcinoma, meningioma, serous ovarian carcinoma and mesothelioma.
Hyperandrogenism with irregular ovulation and polycystic ovaries, usually with insulin resistance and a raised LH to FSH ratio.
A sex cord-stromal tumor of the ovary that secretes androgens, causing virilization.
A fibrous plaque in the tunica albuginea of the penis that causes painful, curved erections.
The fibrous suspensory ligaments of the breast; tumor invasion shortens them and causes skin dimpling.
A neural crest disorder with sensorineural deafness, a white forelock, heterochromic irides and widely spaced inner eye corners.
White speckles around the periphery of the iris, seen in Down syndrome.
The auscultation site at the lower left sternal border, over the right ventricle and tricuspid valve.
The auscultation site at the second intercostal space at the left upper sternal border, over the pulmonary valve.
Aortic stenosis with gastrointestinal bleeding from angiodysplasia, caused by acquired von Willebrand syndrome.
Retinal hemorrhages with pale centers, seen in infective endocarditis.
Painless red macules on the palms and soles from septic emboli in infective endocarditis.
Hoarseness from compression of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve by an enlarged left atrium or aortic arch, as in mitral stenosis.
Golden-brown, beaded rods of asbestos fibers coated with iron and protein in the lung, staining blue with Prussian blue.
Rheumatoid arthritis with pneumoconiosis (coal, silica or asbestos) producing multiple lung nodules.
A form of sarcoidosis with uveitis, parotid enlargement, facial palsy and fever.
Nonciliated secretory cells of the bronchioles that secrete protective proteins, detoxify through cytochrome P450 and act as progenitors; now called club cells.
Shoulder and arm pain, hand weakness and Horner syndrome from an apical lung tumor invading the brachial plexus and sympathetic chain.
Platelet granules storing ADP, ATP, calcium and serotonin, released on activation; deficient in Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome.
Red cells with evenly spaced short spicules (echinocytes), seen in uremia and pyruvate kinase deficiency.
Glycoprotein Ib deficiency causing giant platelets, thrombocytopenia and failed platelet adhesion, with no agglutination in response to ristocetin.
Glycogen storage disease type IV from branching enzyme deficiency, causing abnormal long-chain glycogen, hepatosplenomegaly, cirrhosis and early death.
Modified smooth muscle cells of the afferent arteriole that secrete renin in response to low perfusion pressure or sympathetic stimulation.
Foamy, keratinized patches on the conjunctiva in vitamin A deficiency.
Iron deficiency anemia with esophageal webs and glossitis, causing dysphagia and raising the risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
An antibody-secreting, terminally differentiated B cell with an eccentric clock-face nucleus and perinuclear clearing from the Golgi; the malignant cell of multiple myeloma.
Ciliated glial cells lining the ventricles and central canal that help produce and circulate cerebrospinal fluid.
Reactivation of varicella-zoster virus in the geniculate ganglion, causing facial palsy with vesicles in the ear.
A tuning fork on the midline of the forehead; sound lateralizes toward the affected ear in conductive hearing loss and away from it in sensorineural loss.
A tuning fork compares air and bone conduction; bone conduction louder than air indicates conductive hearing loss.
Dominant angular gyrus lesion causing agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia and left-right confusion.
Bilateral amygdala damage causing hyperorality, hypersexuality, placidity and visual agnosia; seen after herpes simplex encephalitis.
Round, silver-staining tau inclusions in neurons of frontotemporal dementia (Pick disease).
Gastric chief cells secrete pepsinogen and gastric lipase; parathyroid chief cells secrete parathyroid hormone.
A benign, often bilateral parotid tumor in smokers, with cystic spaces, oncocytic epithelium and lymphoid stroma.
A gastric ulcer after brain injury or raised intracranial pressure, driven by vagal hyperstimulation and acid secretion.
Gastric ulcers after brain injury or raised intracranial pressure, driven by vagal hyperstimulation and acid secretion.
A periumbilical nodule of metastatic cancer from an intra-abdominal or pelvic tumor, such as stomach or ovary.
A crunching sound in time with the heartbeat from air in the mediastinum, as in esophageal rupture.
Fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain, the presentation of ascending cholangitis.
The ankle-jerk reflex tested by tapping the Achilles tendon, mediated by S1.
A sequence of head positions that moves displaced otoliths out of the posterior semicircular canal to treat BPPV.
A diagnostic test for BPPV in which the patient is moved from sitting to supine with the head turned; positive if vertigo and nystagmus follow.
Benign mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia from reduced UGT1A1 activity, worsened by fasting or stress.
Hepatic stellate (Ito) cells store vitamin A and lay down collagen in cirrhosis; stellate cells are also inhibitory interneurons in the cerebellar molecular layer.
Eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions of damaged keratin in hepatocytes, typical of alcoholic hepatitis.
A peritoneal fold from the liver to the anterior abdominal wall whose free edge carries the ligamentum teres, the remnant of the umbilical vein.
The portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct running together at the corners of a liver lobule.
The lower edge of the external oblique aponeurosis from the anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle; landmark for inguinal and femoral hernias.
Patient serum is mixed with test red cells to detect free antibodies; used for crossmatching and prenatal screening.
Detects antibodies or complement bound to the patient's own red cells, as in autoimmune hemolytic anemia and hemolytic disease of the newborn.
A distal radius fracture with dorsal displacement ("dinner fork" deformity), usually after a fall on an outstretched hand.
The amount of gas dissolved in a liquid is proportional to its partial pressure; dissolved oxygen is 0.003 times PaO2.
Flexion at the proximal interphalangeal joint with hyperextension at the distal joint, from rupture of the extensor tendon central slip; seen in rheumatoid arthritis.
A first pharyngeal arch neural crest defect causing malar hypoplasia, micrognathia, downslanting eyes and conductive hearing loss.
Flexion deformity of the wrist and fingers from forearm compartment ischemia, classically after supracondylar humerus fracture.
A fracture of the distal humerus above the condyles, common in children; risks injury to the brachial artery and median nerve.
A clinical score for appendicitis combining migratory pain, anorexia, nausea, right lower quadrant tenderness, rebound, fever and leukocytosis.
Liver disease with intrapulmonary vascular dilation and hypoxemia, causing platypnea and orthodeoxia.
Anterior pulling of the tibia with the knee flexed about 20-30 degrees; excess translation indicates an ACL tear.
Holding the wrists flexed for about a minute to reproduce numbness and tingling of carpal tunnel syndrome.
A murmur lasting through systole and into diastole without a break at S2, such as the machine-like murmur of patent ductus arteriosus.
The infectious, metabolically inactive extracellular form of Chlamydia that enters cells and converts to a reticulate body.
The replicating, metabolically active intracellular form of Chlamydia that divides and then reorganizes into elementary bodies.
Eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in poxvirus infections such as smallpox and vaccinia.
Shrunken, eosinophilic apoptotic hepatocytes in viral hepatitis and yellow fever.
A prognostic score for acute pancreatitis using age, WBC, glucose, LDH and AST at admission and changes at 48 hours.
Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (or adult-onset form) with spiking fevers, a salmon-colored rash, arthritis and very high ferritin.
Congenital Zika syndrome: microcephaly, collapsed skull, eye defects and joint contractures after maternal Zika virus infection.
Organelle that modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids, adding mannose-6-phosphate to lysosomal enzymes.
Tennis racket-shaped cytoplasmic organelles in Langerhans cells and Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
An aortic arch anomaly, such as a double aortic arch, that encircles the trachea and esophagus, causing stridor and dysphagia.
Consumptive coagulopathy with severe thrombocytopenia caused by a kaposiform vascular tumor of infancy.
Bruising over the mastoid process, indicating a basilar skull fracture.
Paper that turns blue in the alkaline amniotic fluid (pH 7-7.5), used to detect rupture of membranes.
A qualitative screen for fetomaternal hemorrhage in which Rh-positive fetal cells form rosettes around anti-D coated indicator cells.
An acid elution test that counts fetal hemoglobin-containing red cells in maternal blood to quantify fetomaternal hemorrhage and guide Rh immunoglobulin dosing.
Left shoulder pain from diaphragmatic irritation by blood, as in splenic rupture, referred via the phrenic nerve.
Lymphangiosarcoma arising in chronic lymphedema, classically of the arm after mastectomy.
Reversal of a left-to-right shunt (ASD, VSD, PDA) to right-to-left because of pulmonary hypertension, causing cyanosis, clubbing and polycythemia.
Anemia with large red cells (MCV above 100), from B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol, hypothyroidism or some drugs.
A paradoxical rise in jugular venous pressure on inspiration, seen in constrictive pericarditis and restrictive cardiomyopathy.
An abnormally large submucosal artery, usually in the stomach, that erodes the mucosa and causes sudden massive GI bleeding.
A cirrhosis severity score from bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites and encephalopathy, graded class A to C.
Skin and tissue death from prolonged pressure over a bony prominence, staged I to IV.
Clinical criteria (tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical nodes, fever, no cough) used to estimate the chance of strep pharyngitis.
A ligament from the cervix to the sacrum that supports the uterus; a common site of endometriosis nodules.
Hypotension, distended neck veins and muffled heart sounds, the signs of cardiac tamponade.
Skin and tissue death from prolonged pressure over a bony prominence, staged I to IV.
On ultrasound, a triangular projection of placental tissue between the membranes of a twin pregnancy, indicating dichorionic twins.
A bone fracture from repetitive loading, common in the metatarsals and tibia of runners and recruits; radiographs are often normal early.
Aortoiliac occlusive disease causing buttock and thigh claudication, impotence and absent femoral pulses.
Melanoma depth of invasion, measured in millimeters from the granular layer to the deepest tumor cells; the key prognostic factor.
Septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein after oropharyngeal infection, usually Fusobacterium necrophorum, with septic emboli to the lungs.
Squeezing the calf; absent plantar flexion of the foot indicates Achilles tendon rupture.
Heel pain in active children from inflammation of the calcaneal growth plate at the Achilles insertion.
A Guillain-Barre variant with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and areflexia, associated with anti-GQ1b antibodies.
Neck extension with lateral flexion and downward pressure that reproduces arm pain in cervical radiculopathy.
Hamartomas along the ventricular walls in tuberous sclerosis, often calcified.
A lymphoproliferative disorder with enlarged lymph nodes; the multicentric form is linked to HHV-8 and interleukin-6.
